Most virtual try-on tools render a look and stop. TryProof treats the render as a claim and checks it against your skin. It is a mobile-first web app built on three YouCam APIs.
Skin Analysis scores eight concerns, like redness, texture and dark circles, and Facial Color Tones finds the shade. This is Dev, an AI-generated sample face.
A small rules engine turns those scores into settings for Makeup Virtual Try-On: smoothing, foundation coverage and glow, and under-eye concealer, each with its reason.

Then the rendered image goes back through Skin Analysis, so every concern gets a before and after score. On this face the first render made pores read worse, so TryProof backed the smoothing off, rendered again, and kept the better round. A one-size preset is shown for comparison. The averages are close, so the value is the check, not a bigger number.
The verified settings become a product spec a shopper can use.
Live mode runs your own selfie with your own key. Here is a real run, sped up: upload, skin read, try-on, re-score, verdict. Scores describe how the image reads to the model, not a medical result.
